A.q: What is the way that the mind makes sense of the world?
A.explain: Thinking is the way that the mind makes sense of the world.

A.q: Thinking is classified as what kind of function?
A.explain: Thinking is a higher cognitive function.

A.q: Which type of thinking proceeds on the assumption that there is one single best solution to any problem?
A.explain: Convergent thinking assumes there is one single best solution to any problem.

A.q: Convergent thinking assumes the solution can be arrived at on the basis of what?
A.explain: Convergent thinking assumes the solution can be arrived at on the basis of existing knowledge.

A.q: Which type of thinking is associated with the ability to create or construct something new, novel, or unusual?
A.explain: Divergent or creative thinking is associated with creating or constructing something new, novel, or unusual.

A.q: Divergent thinking looks for new relationships and associations to do what?
options: Describe and interpret the nature of things, events, and situations
Determine the single best solution to any complex problem based on existing knowledge
Judge information according to established personal, professional, or social rules
Separate a whole into its functional parts to discover relationships
A.explain: Divergent thinking looks for new relationships and associations to describe and interpret the nature of things, events, and situations.

A.q: What does it mean to be critical of a text?
options: Question the information and opinions in the text to evaluate or judge its worth overall
Criticize the author in an exclusively negative manner without evaluating the content
Accept all information and opinions as absolute truth without questioning
Ignore the opinions presented in the text and focus only on isolated facts
A.explain: To be critical of a text means you question the information and opinions in the text to evaluate or judge its worth overall.

A.q: Being critical does NOT mean what?
options: Criticizing in an exclusively negative manner
Evaluating the overall worth of information
Questioning opinions presented in a text
Judging the general value of a text
A.explain: To be critical does not mean to criticize in an exclusively negative manner.

A.q: Critical thinking is described as what kind of process?
A.explain: Critical thinking is a self-directed process by which we take deliberate steps to think at the highest level of quality.

A.q: In critical thinking, deliberate steps are taken to think at what level?
options: The most basic level of recall
The most emotional level of response
A.explain: Critical thinking involves taking deliberate steps to think at the highest level of quality.

A.q: Critical thinking involves identifying and analyzing problems. What else does it require?

steps.prompt: After identifying and analyzing problems, what must a critical thinker do?
After seeking and evaluating relevant information, what is the goal?

A.explain: Critical thinking is the ability to identify and analyze problems as well as seek and evaluate relevant information in order to reach an appropriate conclusion.

A.q: Why is critical thinking important for Health Professions Education Students?

steps.prompt: What must Health Professions Education Students do?
Besides making complex decisions, what else must they do?
What ongoing requirement do they have?
options: Complete all coursework requirements as quickly as possible
Follow established clinical protocols without any deviation
Memorize textbook content verbatim for all future exams

A.explain: Health Professions Education Students must make complex decisions, adapt to new situations, and continuously update their knowledge and skills, making critical thinking integral.

A.q: Which of the following are listed as critical thinking skills in the lecture?
A.explain: The critical thinking skills listed are Analyzing, Applying Standards, Discriminating, Information Seeking, Logical Reasoning, and Predicting. Memorizing verbatim is not a critical thinking skill.

A.q: Which critical thinking skill involves separating or breaking a whole into parts to discover their nature, functional, and relationships?
A.explain: Analyzing involves separating or breaking a whole into parts to discover their nature, functional, and relationships.

A.q: The quotes 'I studied it piece by piece' and 'I sorted things out' are associated with which critical thinking skill?
A.explain: These quotes are associated with Analyzing, which involves breaking a whole into parts.

A.q: Which critical thinking skill involves judging according to established personal, professional, or social rules or criteria?
A.explain: Applying Standards means judging according to established personal, professional, or social rules or criteria.

A.q: Which critical thinking skill involves recognizing differences and similarities among things or situations and distinguishing carefully as to category or rank?
A.explain: Discriminating involves recognizing differences and similarities among things or situations and distinguishing carefully as to category or rank.

A.q: The quotes 'I rank ordered the various...' and 'I grouped things together' are associated with which critical thinking skill?
A.explain: These quotes are associated with Discriminating, which involves distinguishing carefully as to category or rank.

A.q: Which critical thinking skill involves searching for evidence, facts, or knowledge by identifying relevant sources?
A.explain: Information Seeking involves searching for evidence, facts, or knowledge by identifying relevant sources.

A.q: Gathering objective, subjective, historical, and current data from relevant sources is part of which critical thinking skill?
A.explain: Gathering objective, subjective, historical, and current data is part of Information Seeking.

A.q: Which critical thinking skill involves drawing inferences or conclusions that are supported in or justified by evidence?
A.explain: Logical Reasoning involves drawing inferences or conclusions that are supported in or justified by evidence.

A.q: The quotes 'I deduced from the information that...' and 'My rationale for the conclusion was...' are associated with which critical thinking skill?
A.explain: These quotes are associated with Logical Reasoning, which involves drawing inferences or conclusions supported by evidence.

A.q: Which critical thinking skill involves envisioning a plan and its consequences?
A.explain: Predicting involves envisioning a plan and its consequences.

A.q: The quotes 'I envisioned the outcome would be...' and 'I was prepared for...' are associated with which critical thinking skill?
A.explain: These quotes are associated with Predicting, which involves envisioning a plan and its consequences.

A.q: Which of the following are listed as barriers to thinking critically?
options: Wanting to know the answers without having to ask questions
A.explain: The barriers listed are misunderstanding, lack of detailed knowledge, and wanting to know the answers without having to ask questions. Gathering information is a critical thinking practice, not a barrier.

A.q: Misunderstanding is a barrier to critical thinking. What causes it?

options: Lack of awareness of the processes involved
Lack of sufficient study time allocated for the subject
Lack of intrinsic motivation to engage with the material
Lack of adequate physical resources or study materials
Thinking critical thinking means making negative comments
Thinking critical thinking requires verbatim memorization of facts
Thinking critical thinking is too difficult for most students
Thinking critical thinking is unnecessary for basic comprehension

A.explain: Misunderstanding can arise due to language or cultural differences, a lack of awareness of the processes involved, or a misunderstanding that critical thinking means making negative comments.

A.q: Lack of detailed knowledge is a barrier to critical thinking. What does this mean?

steps.prompt: What type of knowledge is the problem?

options: Not having read deeply enough around the subject
Having read too much material without any real focus
Having memorized isolated facts without understanding context
Having practical experience only without theoretical background

A.explain: Lack of detailed knowledge refers to superficial knowledge, meaning not having read deeply enough around the subject.

A.q: Critical thinking is aimed at achieving what in any situation?
A.explain: Critical thinking is aimed at achieving the best possible outcomes in any situation.

A.q: To achieve the best possible outcomes, what must critical thinking involve?
options: Gathering and evaluating information from as many different sources
Relying on a single authoritative source of information exclusively
Avoiding asking questions to save time and reach conclusions faster
Accepting superficial knowledge as sufficient for complex decision making
A.explain: To achieve the best possible outcomes, critical thinking must involve gathering and evaluating information from as many different sources.

A.q: Match each critical thinking skill to its description.

rightItems.text: Separating or breaking a whole into parts
Judging according to established rules or criteria
Recognizing differences and similarities among things
Searching for evidence and gathering data from sources
Drawing inferences or conclusions supported by evidence
Envisioning a plan and its consequences

A.explain: Analyzing breaks a whole into parts. Applying Standards judges by rules. Discriminating recognizes differences. Information Seeking gathers data. Logical Reasoning draws supported inferences. Predicting envisions plans and consequences.

A.q: Identify the barriers to thinking critically.

steps.prompt: Which barrier arises due to language or cultural differences, or a lack of awareness of the processes involved?
Which barrier refers to superficial knowledge, meaning not having read deeply enough around the subject?
Which barrier involves wanting to know the answers without doing what?

A.explain: The three barriers are misunderstanding (due to language/culture or process awareness), lack of detailed knowledge (superficial reading), and wanting to know answers without asking questions.

A.q: Match the quotes to their critical thinking skills.

steps.prompt: Which skill is associated with the quote: 'I studied it piece by piece'?
Which skill is associated with the quote: 'I judged it according to...'?
Which skill is associated with the quote: 'I deduced from the information that...'?

A.explain: 'I studied it piece by piece' is Analyzing. 'I judged it according to...' is Applying Standards. 'I deduced from the information that...' is Logical Reasoning.

A.q: Match each type of thinking to its definition.

rightItems.text: Assumes one single best solution based on existing knowledge
Ability to create or construct something new, novel, or unusual
Self-directed process to think at the highest level of quality

A.explain: Convergent thinking assumes one best solution. Divergent thinking creates something new. Critical thinking is a self-directed process for high-quality thought.

A.q: Understanding anything is possible only through which mental activity?
A.explain: There is no way to understand anything except through thinking. Analyzing, predicting, and seeking are specific critical-thinking skills, not the universal way the mind understands.

A.q: Critical thinking is described as the key to what?
A.explain: Critical thinking is the key to resolving problems. Making negative comments is a misunderstanding barrier; avoiding questions is a barrier; envisioning plans is the predicting skill.

A.q: Critical thinking is integral to all of what?
A.explain: Critical thinking is integral to all the things health profession students must do: making complex decisions, adapting to new situations, and updating knowledge and skills. Barriers, skills, and types are other categories.

A.q: Which skill matches 'I knew I needed to lookup/study...' and 'I kept searching for data.'?
A.explain: These quotes match information seeking, which searches for evidence and data. Logical reasoning draws conclusions, predicting envisions plans, and discriminating ranks or groups.

A.q: Critical thinking is described as having what?
A.explain: Critical thinking has many skills to be practiced. One best solution describes convergent thinking; barriers do exist; negative comments are a misunderstanding.
